assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm framework with selection into exporting changed how trade is modeled and measured. It shifted the gains from trade toward reallocation across firms and fed directly into firm-level empirical work and policy analysis. The influence extends well beyond trade into macro, growth and IO.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central, widely recognized contribution. Helpman's work on trade with firm heterogeneity (with Melitz and Yeaple on exports versus FDI) and on broader trade theory is the natural co-credit. Redding is an important extender, especially in quantitative spatial and trade models, but the core idea is better attributed to Melitz and Helpman. Related work by Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and by Hopenhayn, is not on this ballot line and complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation, with the model now textbook material and heavily tested with micro data. Timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Priority and credit relative to Bernard-Jensen and Eaton-Kortum, and to Hopenhayn in the firm-dynamics literature.
Whether the committee prefers the quantitative-trade line (B043) as the better-cited frame.
Trade was recognized with Krugman in 2008, which may reduce the weight of trade as a field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Misallocation as a quantitative explanation of cross-country TFP and income differences created a major research program in macro-development. It gives a disciplined framework linking firm-level distortions to aggregate productivity, and it informs policy on reforms and market frictions.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) is the anchor paper, with Restuccia-Rogerson (2008) as parallel and equally important work. The three-name ceiling on laureates means the Restuccia contribution is in tension with the Hsieh-Klenow credit. Hopenhayn and related firm-dynamics ideas are antecedents.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen-plus years of influence, with extensive replication across countries. There is ongoing debate on measurement error and on how much of the dispersion reflects true distortions.
uncertainties: Measurement-error critiques of dispersion in revenue productivity could weaken the quantitative claims.
Priority between Hsieh-Klenow and Restuccia-Rogerson.
Disclosed connection: the member is a long-running co-author of Klenow. This is disclosed, not adjudicated, and the ranking tries to rest on merit alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based approach to technology, plus evidence on import competition (the China shock), reshaped understanding of wage inequality, polarization and local labor-market adjustment. It is both empirically influential and policy relevant, and it is highly topical given automation and AI.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Katz anchor the technology and skill-premium line (Katz-Murphy, Autor-Katz-Kearney, Autor-Levy-Murnane). Autor, Dorn and Hanson anchor the China shock. The task framework's theoretical core is also tied to Acemoglu and Restrepo, who are not on this ballot line, and Acemoglu already received the 2024 prize, which complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: Decades of evidence on skill-biased change and over a decade on the China shock, with strong replication and some revisions.
uncertainties: Overlap with Acemoglu's task-based work, and with the 2024 prize.
Heterogeneity in the persistence of the China shock's effects.
Choosing three out of four credited names, with Dorn left out.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Weak-instrument diagnostics and identification-robust inference changed everyday applied practice in IV and GMM, fixing a widespread problem in empirical work across fields. This is a methodological contribution with very wide use.
assessment.attribution: Staiger-Stock (1997) is the key diagnostic paper. Stock-Yogo provides critical values and Andrews, Moreira and Stock the robust-testing theory. Moreira's conditional likelihood ratio work is also pivotal, so the three-name cap forces a hard choice. Bound-Jaeger-Baker and Nelson-Startz are precursors.
assessment.maturity: About 25 years of confirmation and now standard practice. Imbens-Angrist-Card already recognized the IV/LATE line in 2021.
uncertainties: Selection among five credited names, with Moreira and Yogo omitted.
Whether the committee sees this as too technical or too close to the already-honored IV line.
Stock also appears on the forecasting ballot line B006, which could dilute the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The empirical and sufficient-statistics approach to optimal taxation connects elasticities of taxable income to welfare analysis and policy design. It has been highly influential in public economics and in tax policy debates.
assessment.attribution: Slemrod was an early and sustained contributor on behavioral responses and avoidance. Saez's optimal-tax and top-income work, and Chetty's sufficient-statistics approach, built the modern framework. Feldstein, who is not on this ballot line, and Mirrlees/Diamond (Mirrlees prized 1996) are important antecedents. Stantcheva is a younger contributor.
assessment.maturity: Two to three decades of the elasticity literature, with newer sufficient-statistics work. Confirmation is mixed because estimates of elasticities are disputed.
uncertainties: Debate over the size and identification of ETI elasticities.
Overlap with the top-income and inequality line (B036) and with Chetty's mobility work (B050), which complicates credit.
Whether the committee judges the sufficient-statistics line mature enough.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Integrating machine learning with causal inference, via double/debiased ML and causal forests, gave practical tools for heterogeneous effects and high-dimensional controls. It is methodologically important and widely adopted in empirical work, policy evaluation and industry.
assessment.attribution: Chernozhukov and coauthors developed double/debiased ML and high-dimensional inference. Athey and Wager developed causal forests and related heterogeneous-effect estimators, with Imbens as an important co-developer outside this ballot line. Wager's role is largely tied to the forest theory.
assessment.maturity: About a decade old, still developing, and with much influence but less long-run validation than older candidates.
uncertainties: Whether a decade of influence is enough for a prize, versus waiting.
Omission of Imbens and others in the ML-causal inference line from the credited names.
Athey also appears in B029, and Chernozhukov in B037, which complicates attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete choice and the estimation of dynamic programs made structural models of forward-looking behavior empirically feasible. They are used across labor, IO, health and education, and they supply the basis for counterfactual policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Rust (1987) is the foundational contribution on nested fixed-point estimation. Keane (with Wolpin) developed simulation-based estimation of finite-horizon models, but Wolpin is not among the credited names, so credit for that line is incomplete. Hotz-Miller conditional choice probabilities are another key antecedent outside this ballot line.
assessment.maturity: About 40 years of methodological development and sustained use.
uncertainties: Omitted credit to Wolpin and to Hotz-Miller makes the laureate set incomplete in representing the contribution.
Structural methods may be judged as less discovery-oriented than empirical findings.
Eckstein's role relative to Keane and Rust.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Present bias, quasi-hyperbolic discounting and reference dependence provided workable formal models of self-control and prospect-theoretic preferences. They shaped behavioral public finance, savings policy and consumption analysis, with applications in household finance and policy design.
assessment.attribution: Laibson's quasi-hyperbolic discounting and Rabin's work on time inconsistency and reference-dependent preferences are central. O'Donoghue-Rabin refine naivete versus sophistication. Koszegi-Rabin built the reference-dependent model. Kahneman and Thaler, plus Strotz, Phelps-Pollak and Tversky, are important antecedents, and behavioral economics was already recognized (Kahneman 2002, Thaler 2017).
assessment.maturity: Twenty-five or more years of work, with strong theory, mixed field evidence for some applications, and ongoing debate on identification of present bias.
uncertainties: Identification of present bias versus other explanations in field data.
Credit allocation among five names and the many antecedents.
Behavioral economics has already been recognized twice, so marginal novelty is arguable.
